name: The Sunny Classroom
pitch: On the first morning at a new school, the classroom is so busy that the child can't find a place to fit, until the child notices a thirsty plant on the windowsill and does what they do every morning at home.
setting: A bright classroom at a new school on the very first morning of the year: a row of coat pegs with picture labels, little tables and chairs, a reading rug, a block corner, a small sink with paper cups, and big windows full of late summer sun. On the sunny windowsill sits a drooping potted plant, thirsty after a hot week in the empty room. At home, a small plant lives on the kitchen windowsill.

supportingCast.name: Nico
supportingCast.role: a new classmate who is shy too and becomes the child's first friend
supportingCast.look: a boy about the child's age with short wavy black hair, a mustard yellow cardigan with a ladybug badge over a blue striped T-shirt, green shorts and red sneakers; he carries nothing

storyBeats: watering the little plant at home every morning
the night before the first day
a busy room where everyone is new
waiting by the coat pegs beside shy Nico
the block corner has no room for one more
a thirsty plant on the windowsill
doing what the child knows how to do
home again with something to tell
powerIdeas: What the child already knows from home is what helps. A favorite color can be the child's lunchbox or the picture on their coat peg, and a favorite thing can be what the child and Nico talk about while the plant drinks.

artDirection.mood: bright and fresh, late summer sun through big classroom windows and crayon colors, busy at first, then calm and warm

contentRules: School is safe and kind: no teasing, no unkind children and nobody gets in trouble.
The grown-up says goodbye at the classroom door because that is the school's rule, and comes back at home time as promised.
The teacher is warm and is simply 'the teacher' unless the family adds the child's real teacher.
The plant perks up slowly over the day after a drink, never by magic.
No school, shop or brand names, and no readable words on signs or labels.

familyParts.grownUp: Walks the child to the classroom door, says goodbye there because that is the school's rule, and comes back at home time as promised.
familyParts.youngerChild: Waves goodbye from the stroller at the classroom door and hears all about the plant at home time.
familyParts.olderChild: Waves from the big kids' line but can't come in, and wants to hear all about the day at home time.
familyParts.withoutGrownUp: Say only 'a grown-up' brings the child to the door: show just a hand waving goodbye, and the same hand waving hello at home time.

starters.title: The Little Plant at Big School
starters.summary: It is your child's very first day at big school. The classroom is busy and loud, everyone is new, and it is hard to find a place to fit.
starters.idea: On the first day at big school, the grown-up must say goodbye at the door and the teacher is busy greeting each family, so nobody notices the child. Waiting by the coat pegs to be asked to play fails: everyone is new and busy, and Nico at the next peg is too shy to speak. Joining the block corner fails too: every block is already in a tower. Then the child spots a plant drooping on the windowsill, thirsty after a hot week. Like the plant at home (shown at the start), it needs a slow drink, and the child knows how. Nico comes to help, and by home time the plant and the child both stand taller.
